heroBody: The Sony WH-1000XM6 and the Bose QuietComfort Ultra Headphones are the two flagship noise-cancelling headphones Singapore shoppers actually cross-shop, and in Singapore they are priced close enough that the decision comes down to fit and use case rather than sticker price. Both are sold in S$ locally by stereo specialists, Challenger and FairPrice alongside marketplace stores, and both drop measurably during 9.9, 11.11 and 12.12 platform sales. This page pulls live Singapore listings from BuyWhere's catalog every few minutes so you can compare today's real floor price for each, and see which retailer currently holds it.

highlights.title: The XM6 finally folds
highlights.body: Sony's biggest change over the XM5 is the return of a folding hinge, which matters more than it sounds if you carry the headphones in a bag on the MRT. The XM5's fixed shape forced a large flat case; the XM6 packs smaller while keeping the wider ear cups and softer cushions that fixed the XM5's clamp complaints.

highlights.title: Bose still wins the commute, Sony wins the flight
highlights.body: The QC Ultra's noise cancellation leans harder on voices and cabin midrange, which makes hawker centres and open offices feel quieter; the XM6's low-frequency damping is at its best against MRT rumble and airplane drone. Both are excellent — the honest difference is smaller than forum arguments suggest, and fit decides more of it than the DSP does.

highlights.title: Local warranty matters at this price
highlights.body: Both headphones carry a one-year local warranty when bought from an authorised Singapore retailer (Challenger, stereo specialists, FairPrice listings of local sets). Parallel imports appear cheaper on marketplaces, but neither Sony nor Bose Singapore services grey sets under warranty, and XM6 hinge repairs are not cheap out of pocket.

adviceSectionTitle: How to choose and pay the least in Singapore
advicePoints: Try both on before buying: the XM6's clamp and the QC Ultra's cushion pressure suit different head shapes, and no spec sheet tells you which you can wear for a six-hour flight. Challenger and stereo stores in Sim Lim Square usually have both on display.

If you take calls in shared spaces, lean Bose — the QC Ultra's microphone wind and voice handling is still the benchmark. If you mostly listen to music on commutes, the XM6's LDAC and EQ flexibility give it the edge on Android.

Time the purchase: both models see real drops during 9.9, 10.10, 11.11 and 12.12 campaigns on Shopee and Lazada, and Fairprice and specialist stores occasionally match. The live table below shows today's floor, not the sale floor.
Watch for earbud listings mixed into results: the QC Ultra Earbuds are a different product at a different price. Confirm the listing says 'Headphones' before comparing prices.
Check 'local set' on the listing before buying the cheapest offer — a warranty claim on a parallel import goes back to the shop, not Sony or Bose Singapore.
faqSectionTitle: Sony WH-1000XM6 vs Bose QC Ultra in Singapore — common questions

faqs.question: Is the Sony WH-1000XM6 or Bose QuietComfort Ultra better for MRT commutes in Singapore?
faqs.answer: Both mute MRT rumble well. The XM6's low-frequency cancellation has a slight edge against track drone, while the QC Ultra dampens cabin chatter and hawker-centre noise better. If your commute is crowded and talkative, Bose; if it is long and droning, Sony.

faqs.question: Which is cheaper in Singapore right now?
faqs.answer: Street prices move weekly and cross during sales; check the live price table above for today's floor on each model from Singapore retailers. Historically the two land in the same mid-flagship band in S$, with sale-day gaps of tens of dollars rather than hundreds.

faqs.question: Do parallel-import XM6 or QC Ultra headphones get local warranty in Singapore?
faqs.answer: No. Sony Singapore and Bose Singapore honour the one-year warranty only on local sets from authorised retailers. Grey-market listings are cheaper precisely because warranty claims go back to the shop that sold them.

faqs.question: Can I use the WH-1000XM6 or QC Ultra with an iPhone?
faqs.answer: Yes. Both pair as standard Bluetooth headphones with any iPhone, and Bose supports Apple's find-my style tracking via SimpleSync ecosystems, but Sony's LDAC hi-res codec is Android-only. iPhone owners lose nothing important on either; Android owners get a small audio edge with the Sony.

categoryIntro.heading: Why this comparison matters in Singapore
categoryIntro.body: Singapore buyers pay a premium for flagship headphones but also get one of the densest competitive retail markets in the region: authorised chains, stereo specialists, Fairprice and marketplace official stores all stock both models, and prices diverge by tens of dollars within the same week. That density makes a fixed 'winner' article useless within days, which is why this page reads live listings for both models side by side and leaves the verdict to fit, use case and today's price.
